title: Lahore: Gates, Mosques & City
summary: A fixed route through Delhi Gate, Shahi Hammam and Wazir Khan Mosque, connecting an urban threshold, a historic bathhouse and a living sacred landmark.
body: This curated planning route approaches Lahore through the relationship between streets and institutions. Delhi Gate introduces the historic city's edge and the passage into its commercial fabric. The nearby Shahi Hammam provides a different setting for considering water, service and architectural conservation. Wazir Khan Mosque then brings the route into a major sacred and urban ensemble. These are three separate Heritage records, not interchangeable examples of a single monument type. The fixed itinerary follows this sequence. Current opening arrangements, worship requirements, walking conditions and group access are checked before departure.

title: Rohtas & Taxila: Landscapes of Power and Learning
summary: A two-day heritage journey linking Rohtas Fort with Taxila’s archaeological landscape, departing from Lahore.
body: Rohtas Fort and Taxila support different ways of understanding the northern Punjab landscape. The fort invites close attention to walls, gateways and the organisation of a defensible place. Taxila is a serial archaeological property whose settlements and religious sites should be understood together, not reduced to a single map pin or monument. This route therefore treats Taxila as one canonical Heritage Place with multiple documented components. The fixed itinerary visits selected components of Taxila alongside Rohtas Fort. Travel begins in Lahore; transport, overnight arrangements and practical site access form part of the departure information.

title: Indus Cities & Thatta: Archaeology, Memory and Craft
summary: A four-day journey connecting Moenjodaro, Makli and Shah Jahan Mosque, with travel from Lahore.
body: This planning route brings together an archaeological city, a major funerary landscape and a living mosque without presenting them as one continuous historical episode. Moenjodaro asks questions about urban organisation and the interpretation of excavated remains. Makli offers a different encounter with monuments, burial traditions and remembered political communities around Thatta. Shah Jahan Mosque introduces another architectural and devotional setting. Each Place has its own source record and designation; the mosque is not described here as an inscribed World Heritage property. The fixed journey brings these three places together, with travel from Lahore and practical arrangements shared for each departure. The related records below provide context while keeping the three places distinct.
